title: Company Alignment Heatmap and Decision Heuristics (v0.1)
content:
PURPOSE:
This doc is a lightweight, annotated heatmap + heuristics deck we want to surface in the June company sync and use as the canonical input to Q3 OKR scoping. Goal: give execs and team leads a single, prioritized view of candidate initiatives and a set of simple decision rules so cross-functional tradeoffs are fast and consistent.

CONTEXT + WHY NOW:
- We’ve had a flood of proposals across product, infra, and go-to-market after the Q2 capacity ramp. Need to compress decision latency going into recruiting and budget cycles.
- Observed problem: parallel projects with similar customer impact are competing for limited infra and SRE capacity.
- This doc is intentionally compact — not the spec for each project. It should point to owners and the short list of follow-ups for the all-hands breakout.

HOW TO USE THIS DOCUMENT (for leads / execs):
1) Review the heatmap quadrant placements and raise edge cases.
2) Apply the heuristics to any initiative that lands close to the boundary.
3) For items accepted into the top band, expect a 2-week scoping sprint and a one-page operational plan (owner, SLOs, first 3 milestones).

HEATMAP OVERVIEW (candidate initiatives) — visual layout described in text for quick drive consumption:
- X-axis: Customer impact / revenue velocity (left low → right high)
- Y-axis: Operational risk / infra cost (bottom low → top high)
Top-right (High impact, High cost/risk):
  - Dedicated Capacity Tiering (product + infra) — owner: Miguel R. — outcome: 25% latency improvement for reserved workloads; cost predictability.
  - Private Deployment Audit & Harden (security) — owner: Sophie L. — outcome: SOC2+ readiness for large regulated accounts.
Top-left (High impact, Low cost/risk):
  - Streaming SDK ergonomic fixes (DX) — owner: David R. — outcome: reduce onboarding time by 40% for new customers.
  - Model Catalog tagging & curated defaults (product) — owner: Asha P. — outcome: fewer support escalations, faster time-to-prod.
Bottom-right (Low impact, High cost/risk):
  - Experimental multi-GPU sharding prototype — deferred to R&D backlog unless ROI improves.
Bottom-left (Low impact, Low cost/risk):
  - Internal templates refresh (docs) — low priority, scheduled as part of onboarding backlog.

PRIORITIZATION BAND (how we slice the heatmap into three bands):
- Band A (Top priority): Items with projected month-to-month MRR or strategic unblock AND <12 week engineering ramp (or SLA-driven must-do).
- Band B (Secondary): Items with meaningful customer experience improvement but either >12 week runway or high infra dependency.
- Band C (Backlog): Nice-to-haves, research spikes, and purely exploratory experiments.

DECISION HEURISTICS (simple, operational rules for rapid triage):
1) If an initiative unlocks >$50k ARR in Q4 and requires <= 2 FTEs to launch, auto-promote to Band A candidate.
2) If an initiative reduces per-token cost by >=10% at production load, prioritize ahead of non-cost initiatives of similar impact.
3) If a project increases tail latency risk for Hosted API customers, require an explicit rollback/runbook before approving canary.
4) Cross-team resource contention: projects that need >25% of a single infra team's capacity in a quarter require an exec-level reallocation decision (not just peer planning).
5) Security/compliance requests (private deployments, audit readiness) are first-class: if a customer contract has a signed letter of intent tied to compliance, escalate to Band A.

PROPOSED OKR CANDIDATES (draft wording for the OKR cadence conversation):
- Objective: Make Redwood predictably production-grade for regulated customers
  - KR1: Complete hardening/attestation checklist for Private deployments with three customer pilot signoffs by EOY
  - KR2: Reduce mean time to recovery for Reserved pools from 32m -> 8m
- Objective: Reduce per-token unit cost for common customer patterns
  - KR1: Ship prefix caching improvements that yield >=12% token cost reduction on sample workloads
  - KR2: Provide two quantized model variants in the catalog with perf profiles and automated routing rules
- Objective: Improve developer-first experience for embedding & streaming use cases
  - KR1: SDK streaming latency SLA docs and two sample apps (mobile + backend) launched
  - KR2: Decrease new-customer integration time from signup -> prod by 40% measured on NPS follow-on metrics

TIMELINE (high level, for company sync and follow ups):
- Week 0 (All-hands): present heatmap + split into breakouts (platform, product, customer success). Capture immediate objections.
- Week 1–2: Band A owners run 2-week scoping sprints; produce one-pagers and initial risk/runbook drafts.
- Week 3: Exec review & commit decisions for resource/heads allocations.
- Week 4: Public OKR publish + team-level planning kickoff.

STAKEHOLDER ASKS (for the all-hands):
- Engineering leads: flag any Band A items that will consume >25% of an infra team's quarter capacity.
- Product: confirm the top 3 customer-facing metrics we will use to measure impact (latency p95, onboarding time, demo-to-trial conversion).
- SRE & Observability: outline the rollback criteria and monitoring owners for each Band A item by end of Week 2.
- Sales & CS: identify any near-term deals tied to compliance work and share LOIs by Day 3.

RISKS & MITIGATIONS (short register):
- Risk: Overcommitment of infra capacity → Mitigation: reserve a 25% buffer in Dedicated rollout plan; require cross-team tradeoff doc for any buffer borrow.
- Risk: Quality regressions from model swaps during quantization → Mitigation: automated evals + customer-specific prompt regression alerts before rollout.
- Risk: Conflicting GTM asks (multiple teams needing start-of-quarter demos) → Mitigation: demo calendar and one-pager prioritization committee (weekly).

OPEN QUESTIONS (for the breakout sessions):
- What exact threshold should we use for "strategic unblock" vs. pure revenue? (proposal: LOI or >$50k Q4).
- Is the 12-week engineering ramp cutoff too optimistic given current hiring pace?
- How do we balance small high-velocity wins vs. one or two big platform bets from an engineering morale and hiring signal perspective?

NEXT STEPS (owners called out):
- Asha P.: finalize heatmap graphics and upload to Confluence (INF-742) — due 2025-06-15.
- Miguel R.: draft Dedicated Tiering one-pager and initial cost model — due 2025-06-23.
- Sophie L.: produce compliance readiness checklist & pilot candidate list — due 2025-06-20.
- David R.: compile SDK ergonomic quick wins + measurement plan — due 2025-06-22.

APPENDIX / LINKS:
- Quick links: confluence://page/INF-742-align-heatmap, JIRA:INF-1258 (resource prioritization board), https://github.com/redwood-inference/roadmap/pull/42
- Suggested reading: Evaluations dashboard (internal), recent customer postmortem on Dedicated pool outage (SRE doc link).

NOTES TO SELF / WORKING THOUGHTS:
- Keep the all-hands breakout lightweight — the goal is alignment, not final scoping.
- We should push a short pulse survey after the sync to capture whether the heuristics felt reasonable to team leads.
- If pushed for time in the all-hands, run a quick poll: choose top 2 initiatives per functional area — use this as tie-break for Band A assignments.

END OF DOC (v0.1 draft)
